Answer: C) Spontaneous pneumomediastinum with subcutaneous emphysema  
Reason: The red arrows in Figure 1a (AP view) point to linear lucencies tracking along the mediastinal borders—especially paratracheal and aorticopulmonary window—without pleural edge displacement; Figure 1b (lateral view) confirms air outlining the anterior and posterior mediastinum (including retrosternal and prevertebral regions) but no visceral pleural line, ruling out pneumothorax; subcutaneous emphysema is indicated by the yellow arrows in Figure 1a (soft-tissue lucency in neck/upper chest), consistent with air dissecting from mediastinum to subcutaneous tissues—classic for spontaneous pneumomediastinum after forceful coughing.
